issues.display_title: Issue #459: Update List POTD and Detail POTD
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/07/26

✅ Implementation: Broadcast Viewer Access

Overview

This implementation updates the broadcast notification APIs so the viewer role can access public broadcast and POTD data without requiring a full user profile lookup.

Previously these actions assumed a logged-in user role and called UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt). That fails for viewer because the auth middleware assigns viewer requests a generated encrypt value and an empty userId.

Routes Updated

  • GET /notification/list-broadcast
  • GET /notification/list-potd
  • GET /notification/list-broadcast-bookmark/:slug
  • GET /notification/detail-broadcast-post/:slug

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
  3. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcastBookmark.go
  4. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/DetailBroadcastPost.go

Technical Details

1. Role Validation

Some API updated action now accepts both roles:

if role != "user" && role != "viewer" {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}

This keeps non-broadcast roles blocked while allowing viewer access.

2. Viewer-safe User Data Handling

The UserDatas lookup now runs only for role == "user":

if role == "user" {
	userData := UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt)
	// load last_login and user-specific block lists
}

For viewer, the endpoint skips user profile lookup and uses a generated lastLogin timestamp for encrypted response metadata.

3. Filtering Behavior

All roles still apply the global deactivated-user filter:

notInEncrypt = deactiveUser

For user, the endpoint also appends user-specific blocked users and blocked posts where supported:

notInEncrypt = append(deactiveUser, blockUser...)

This keeps the existing logged-in user privacy behavior while making viewer requests independent from user-specific Redis keys.

4. Support-only Filter

The sp=true support-personal filter remains restricted. Viewer requests with sp=true return unauthorized because viewer has no real user profile or support email:

if role == "viewer" {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}

5. Encrypted Response Shape

The ec == "true" branch now follows a single-return pattern. It replaces responses with the encrypted payload, adds e4 for viewer requests, and returns once at the end:

if ec == "true" {
	MySecret, _ := Functions.KeyEncrypt(lastLogin, encrypt)
	rowDatasSlice := []interface{}{MySecret, lastLogin, 0, responses}
	encText, _ := Functions.EncryptResult(rowDatasSlice, "success", true, 200)
	responses = map[string]interface{}{
		"messages": "...",
		"cry":      encText,
		"ls":       Functions.EpochTime(lastLogin),
	}
	if role == "viewer" {
		responses["e4"] = encrypt
	}
}

return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(responses)

Backward Compatibility

  • Existing user role behavior remains unchanged for block filters and encrypted responses.
  • Existing route paths and query parameters remain unchanged.
  • Viewer access is limited to public broadcast data. User-specific filters are skipped only because viewer has no user account context.
  • sp=true remains unavailable to viewer.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: passed.

Description

  • Allowed access for viewer type Post & Bookmark.

Route :

  • /notification/list-broadcast
  • /notification/list-potd
  • notification/list-broadcast-bookmark/:slug
  • /notification/detail-broadcast-post/:slug

issues.display_title: Issue #460: Add Status Published for API List Bookmarks
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/07/26

✅ Implementation: List Bookmarks Published Status

Overview

This implementation addresses GitHub Task #460 by adding a published status flag to the folder_bookmark object returned by the Detail / Publish Bookmark response.

The client can now determine whether the current bookmark folder has already been published without checking another endpoint.

API

  • Endpoint: GET /bookmark/list/:sid
  • Example: GET /bookmark/list/ldd7110c807-2026070204434800?limit=12&page=1

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/ListBookmarks.go

Technical Details

1. Folder Query Update

The ListBookmarks folder lookup now selects the is_published column from the folder_bookmark table:

Select("id, name, slug, is_published")

The value is read into folderPublished and used when building the response metadata.

2. Response Shape Update

The folder_bookmark response object now includes:

{
  "folder_name": "Example Folder",
  "folder_slug": "ldd7110c807-2026070204434800",
  "published": true
}

For pw=false, the response keeps the existing ID-based shape and also includes the same published status:

{
  "folder_id": "folder-uuid",
  "folder_name": "Example Folder",
  "published": true
}

3. Shared Response Builder

A helper function was added in ListBookmarks.go:

func buildFolderBookmarkResponse(folderId, folderSlug, folderName string, published bool, includeID bool) map[string]interface{}

This keeps the normal and pw=false response shapes consistent and prevents duplicating the published field logic.

Backward Compatibility

  • Existing folder_name and folder_slug fields remain unchanged.
  • Existing pw=false behavior remains unchanged except for the added published field.
  • No route, request parameter, authentication, or database schema changes were required.

Verification

Ran:

Result: passed.

Description

Add a "published" status to the Detail / Publish Bookmark response so the client can tell whether a bookmark folder has been published.

issues.display_title: Issue #385: Validate Published Folder Bookmark for Pick of the Day Bookmark Flow
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/07/26

✅ Implementation: Pick of the Day Bookmark Published Filter

Scope

  • Target file: src/Action/V1/Broadcast/PickOfTheDay.go
  • Target flow: PickOfTheDay with type = bookmark
  • Requirement: folder bookmark must be published before it can be sent as Pick of the Day.

Changes

  • Added Where("fb.is_published = ?", true) to the folder_bookmark AS fb query in the bookmark branch.
  • Kept post flow unchanged. Post publish validation still uses posts.is_publish = true only in the type = post branch.
  • Kept existing post visibility check from joined bookmark posts unchanged.
  • No new helper, struct-level validation, or test file added.

Expected Behavior

  • Published folder bookmark: query can return rows and continue existing notification flow.
  • Unpublished folder bookmark: query returns no rows and existing response remains Bookmark Not Found.
  • type = post: unaffected.

Verification

  • Run: go test ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast
  • Expected: command passes.

Description:
Update src/Action/V1/Broadcast/PickOfTheDay.go so Pick of the Day with type = bookmark only processes published folder bookmarks.

Scope:

  • Only update the bookmark branch in PickOfTheDay.
  • Add query filter:
    Where("fb.is_published = ?", true)
  • Do not change type = post flow.
  • Do not add post publish validation inside bookmark flow.
  • Keep existing joined post visibility validation unchanged.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Published folder bookmark can continue existing Pick of the Day notification flow.
  • Unpublished folder bookmark is not returned by the query and falls through existing Bookmark Not Found response.
  • type = post behavior remains unchanged.
  • go test ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #386: Refactor MentionPosts Module to Use GORM Models
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/07/26

✅ Implementation: MentionPosts Module Refactoring

This document tracks the execution details for the MentionPosts module refactoring.

Phase 1: MentionPost.go

  • Target File: src/Action/V1/MentionPosts/MentionPost.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added the Models import so the endpoint can use existing GORM model types.
    • Replaced raw Config.DB.Exec("DELETE FROM mention_post WHERE post_id = ?", postId) with Config.DB.Where("post_id = ?", postId).Delete(&Models.MentionPost{}).
    • Replaced raw Config.DB.Exec("DELETE FROM notifications WHERE post_id = ? AND notification_type = 'mentions'", postId) with Config.DB.Where("post_id = ? AND notification_type = ?", postId, "mentions").Delete(&Models.Notifications{}).
    • Kept delete logic inline in the handler because the operations are only used once.
    • Preserved existing response messages and status codes.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Verification

  • Ran go test ./src/Action/V1/MentionPosts.
  • Result: passed with no test files.

Background

The MentionPosts module removes mention records and mention notifications with raw SQL DELETE statements. Refactoring these deletes to use existing GORM models keeps the module aligned with the recent Notifications refactor and avoids manual SQL for simple model-based operations.

Objective

Refactor src/Action/V1/MentionPosts/MentionPost.go to use existing GORM models for deleting mention post data and related mention notifications.

APIs to Refactor

  • MentionPost: Replace raw DELETE FROM mention_post WHERE post_id = ? with Config.DB.Where(...).Delete(&Models.MentionPost{}).
  • MentionPost: Replace raw DELETE FROM notifications WHERE post_id = ? AND notification_type = 'mentions' with Config.DB.Where(...).Delete(&Models.Notifications{}).

Acceptance Criteria

  • No raw SQL DELETE queries remain in src/Action/V1/MentionPosts/MentionPost.go.
  • The module uses existing models: Models.MentionPost and Models.Notifications.
  • The refactor does not introduce extra utility functions for one-off delete operations.
  • The endpoint behavior remains unchanged for successful mention removal and existing error responses.
  • The code successfully compiles without unused imports.
